title: the_understudy_who_knew_my_lines
display_title: My theater understudy quit the week of opening night -- because of something I said in my sleep
beats: My understudy quit four days before opening night, and she wouldn't tell the director why.
I was the lead, 22, first real role, and she'd shadowed every rehearsal for six weeks straight.
We'd started sharing a dressing room during tech week, and I talked in my sleep on the couch between run-throughs.
She heard me say something during a nap on day three, and her face went white and she wouldn't look at me after.
I asked her, point blank, what I said -- she just said, 'You knew my sister's name. I never told you my sister's name.'
She quit that night, blocked me everywhere, and opening night I went on with no understudy at all.
What do you think I said?
